fatal_errors: The proposed Nb addition and aging treatment are not supported by any cited evidence specific to Nb-modified AlCoCrFeNi2.1; formation of the asserted nanoscale Nb-rich interfacial precipitates is assumed rather than evidenced.

The response proposes a coupled composition-plus-heat-treatment intervention, despite the request for a single intervention, and lacks factorial controls needed to separate the effects of Nb, solutionizing, and aging.
The claimed corrosion improvement and passivation mechanism have no direct support in the cited studies.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the relevant strength, creep, ductility, thermal-stability, and corrosion objectives and invokes generally plausible precipitation-strengthening and coarsening concepts. However, it does not reconstruct the demonstrated Zr-alloying intervention or its composition-dependent mechanical and corrosion optima. None of the cited papers establishes that Nb forms the proposed precipitates in this alloy, improves its passivation, or remains compatible with the lamellar eutectic structure. E1 concerns Y/Hf-doped laser-clad coatings under 900 °C molten-salt corrosion, E2 characterizes the unmodified alloy, and E3 concerns thermomechanical processing of a different HEA and even warns that incoherent precipitates can reduce ductility. The experiment includes useful microscopy and property measurements, but its control is heat-treated while the stated baseline is as-cast, so it cannot directly establish improvement over the starting material or attribute improvement separately to Nb and heat treatment. Test environments, statistical criteria, thermal-cycle protocols, loads, corrosion electrolyte, and quantitative success thresholds are also unspecified.
